title: Cancel Twin Letters
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters. Whenever two equal letters stand next to each other, they cancel: both are removed and the pieces on either side join up. That join can create a new equal pair, which cancels too.

Keep cancelling until no two neighbouring letters are equal, and return what is left. The result does not depend on the order of cancelling. It may be the empty string.

examples.why: "bb" cancels, leaving "caad"; then "aa" cancels, leaving "cd". One pass that only removes the original pairs would stop at "caad".
Three y's in a row: one pair cancels and one y is left. Removing every letter that has a twin neighbour would give "xz".
"bb" cancels, then "aa" meets and cancels. Nothing is left.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: After a pair cancels, the only new pair that can form is right where the gap closed. What do you need to remember to check it?
Read the string left to right and keep the letters that survive so far. The new letter can only cancel with the last survivor.
Use the result itself as a stack: if the incoming letter equals the top, pop; otherwise push.

explain.intuition:
When a pair cancels, the letters that meet are the one just before the pair and the one just after it. So if you read left to right and keep the surviving letters so far, a new letter can only ever cancel with the last survivor. That is exactly a stack.

Push each letter; if it equals the top, pop instead. The stack always holds a string with no equal neighbours, and at the end it is the answer. It is the same move as an undo history where an action and its exact inverse wipe each other out.
steps: Create an empty stack (an array of characters).
For each letter c of s: if the stack is not empty and its top equals c, pop.
Join the stack into a string and return it.
pitfalls: Making a single pass that removes the pairs in the original string, then stopping. New pairs appear after removal, like in "cabbad".
Removing whole runs of equal letters. A run of three leaves one letter behind.
Rebuilding the string with slice after every removal, which costs O(n) each time and O(n²) overall.

solutions.title: Remove a pair and rescan
solutions.idea: Find any equal neighbours, cut them out, and start over until nothing changes.

solutions.title: Survivors on a stack
solutions.idea: A new letter can only cancel with the last surviving one, so keep the survivors on a stack.

followups: Letters now cancel only in runs of exactly k equal neighbours. What extra value does each stack entry need?
Do it in place with O(1) extra memory on a character array, using a write pointer.
lcTitle: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
